full_details: You slept, woke in the dark hour, and slept again. In the waking you wrote the Christmas letter at the table, one candle, and you did not seal it. Anne is told you will not come, and she is told not to look for you at the door. The quarter's sixty shillings goes Thursday with Hobbins, with oranges, a sugar-loaf, cinnamon, raisins, prunes, the russet Mistress Ansell chose and you paid for, and a groat for each child. One thing for each of them is not named. Joan's is not the russet. You did not untie the private leaves. At St Helen's the sermon ran to fourteenthly, and in the porch he would not give you the rest of it. You told her the house should not expect you on the day. She will not bake on a rumour. After the evening prayers in the kitchen you worked the weaver's head as a joiner would. The ears are too long. The jaw must move or the voice will be lost in it. The margin asks his father for canvas and paste, and for light. The page is funny before it is beautiful. The cat was put off the leaf.
one_sentence: You woke between two sleeps, wrote home that Christmas is Richmond, and after evening prayer drew an ass's head whose jaw has to move.
title: Wrote the Christmas letter and drew a jaw that moves
